chunks: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

A woman from my household made a bequest to me from her wealth and instructed that a slave be emancipated on her behalf, that hajj be performed, and that charity be given. But that amount was not sufficient, so I asked Abū Ḥanīfah, and he said: It should be made into three parts: one-third for hajj, one-third for manumission, and one-third for charity.

Then I entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said to him: A woman from my family died and made a bequest to me of one-third of her wealth, and instructed that a slave be emancipated on her behalf, that hajj be performed on her behalf, and that charity be given on her behalf; then I examined it, and it was not sufficient.

So he عليه السلام said: “Begin with hajj, for it is an obligation from among the obligations of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and make what remains into one portion for manumission and one portion for charity.”
So I informed Abū Ḥanīfah of the statement of Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and he withdrew from his opinion and adopted the statement of Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.

key_terms.أَوْصَتْ: she made a bequest or will
key_terms.بِثُلُثِ: with one-third; referring to the bequeathable third of the estate
key_terms.ٱلصَّدَقَةِ: charity given on behalf of the deceased
key_terms.ٱلْحَجِّ: hajj performed on behalf of the deceased
key_terms.ٱلْعِتْقِ: manumission or emancipation of a slave

ai.seo_question: If a deceased person bequeaths wealth for hajj, manumission, and charity, but the amount is insufficient, which should be given priority?
ai.summary: This hadith explains how a bequest should be carried out when the available amount is insufficient to fulfill all requested acts. Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام gives priority to hajj because it is an obligatory duty, and then the remainder is distributed between manumission and charity. The report also shows the legal authority of the Imam عليه السلام in clarifying the proper ruling.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5491 - Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Muawiyah ibn Ammar who said:

A woman from my family entrusted me with her wealth and instructed that emancipation (of slaves) be made on her behalf, that Hajj be performed, and that charity be given. However, the amount left was insufficient to cover all that.
I consulted Abu Hanifah, and he said: "It should be divided into three parts - one-third for Hajj, one-third for emancipation, and one-third for charity."

Then I went to Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) and said to him:
"A woman from my family passed away and entrusted me with one-third of her wealth, instructing that Hajj be performed on her behalf, emancipation be made, and charity be given. But the amount was not enough to fulfill all these."
Imam (as) said: "Start with Hajj, for it is an obligation from the obligations of Allah (swt), the Exalted. Then divide what remains - part of it for emancipation and part for charity."
I informed Abu Hanifah of the statement of Abu Abdullah (as), and he withdrew his previous opinion and accepted the guidance of Abu Abdullah (as).
